messages:
mike: Quick question — I'm drafting a checklist for the hosting-adapter shim that bridges Hosted / Dedicated / Private. Can we list the minimum runtime guarantees we require from each side? e.g., auth token shape, streaming semantics, model fallback codes, KV cache expectations.

ashley: +1. Minimal guarantees I'd expect: idempotent request IDs, streaming chunk markers, an explicit 'not-supported' error code for unsupported model variants, and header passthrough for traces.

jordan: Also add backpressure signal semantics (HTTP 429 vs connection-level pause), and a retry table that we all agree on. We had ambiguity on retriable errors in last week's incident.

greg: Note: runtime can't preserve KV cache across certain quantized model variants. Adapters should be tolerant of cache drops and retry/continue without panicking. Add an opt-in telemetry tag when cache is cold.

mike: Good point. I'll add a checklist item: "cache loss acceptable; adapter must tag requests with `cache_warm=false` when falling back." Any thoughts on auth/tenant mapping for Private (customer KMS assertions) vs Hosted API keys?

leah: Private control plane will present a signed tenant assertion header `X-Tenant-Assertion` (signed by customer HSM). Hosted uses `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`. Adapter should normalize both into an internal `X-Internal-Tenant` claim for downstream.

ashley: Example header mapping to include in docs:
```
Hosted: Authorization: Bearer <api_key>
Private: X-Tenant-Assertion: <signed-jwt>
Internal: X-Internal-Tenant: <tenant_id>
```

mike: Observability notes: we need consistent trace propagation and sampling parity across modes. If an adapter creates a trace, mark it so we can filter later.

ryan: Add requirement: adapter MUST forward `traceparent` and `baggage`. If absent, generate a new trace and set `adapter_generated=true` tag. Also include `tenant_id` and `hosting_mode` in span attributes.

mike: What about surface for fallbacks? We need explicit mapping rules when Hosted model isn't available and we route to Dedicated or Private variants (or lower-capacity model). How do we signal quality/regression to callers?

jordan: Suggest: adapters should return a `fallback_reason` field when routing downgraded, plus a `model_variant` and `expected_quality_delta` (float). Keep it optional but recommended for telemetry.

leah: Operational caveat: Private sidecars sometimes return 403 with body `{"reason":"kms-unavailable"}`. In practice that's a transient condition and we retry for a short window. Recommend mapping that to 503 at the adapter layer so clients treat it as transient.

ashley: I'll draft an error-code matrix in the RFC. Proposed shorthand for retries: 429, 502, 503 => retry with exponential backoff; 400/422 => do not retry; 403 with `kms-unavailable` => treat as 503.

mike: Poll: thumbs-up if you agree with the matrix and header mappings. I'll turn this into a tiny RFC and a checklist for the runtime-adapters repo. Link: <https://redwood-internal/arch/drafts/shim-checklist>

ashley: :thumbsup: I can take the exact error-code matrix and examples for the RFC.

jordan: I'll own the retry table and include sample client pseudocode.

greg: Add tests: 1) header normalization unit test, 2) streaming chunk boundary test, 3) cache-warm flag propagation test.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Created RFC draft branch `shim-checklist` and added reviewers: @ashley @jordan @mike.

mike: Thanks — I'll update the draft with the mapping rules and tests, and then request a staged canary rollout for the adapter.

leah: One last ops note: please include a clear rollback plan in the RFC. Private customers want an explicit `reject` path if adapter mapping fails rather than silent fallback.

mike: Roger. Adding a rollback step and an explicit `adapter_rejects_on_mapping_failure` toggle (default: false for hosted, true for private).
